The Verses of the Elder Nadīkassapa:
“Truly, for my benefit the Buddha has come to the Nerañjarā River;”
Having heard his Dhamma,
I abandoned wrong view;
I performed various sacrifices, both high and low.
I offered the fire sacrifice,
imagining, "This is purity"—
a blind worldling.
Falling into the thicket of views,
deluded by dogmatic adherence,
I imagined impurity to be purity.
Blinded and ignorant,
my wrong view has been abandoned and all states of existence have been shattered.
I offer oblations to the fire of those worthy of offerings;
I pay homage to the Tathāgata.
All delusions have been abandoned by me.
The craving for existence has been shattered;
the wandering through births is exhausted;
there is now no further becoming.
… The Elder Nadīkassapa …
